I hold a Master's degree in Microbiology from **ETH Zürich**, with a focus on
mycology and biocontrol. Before my PhD I spent several years in agricultural
research — most of it at **Agroscope**, the Swiss Federal Agricultural Research
Station — working on optimising mycopesticide production and managing pests and
plant pathogens in fruit and arable crops.

Driven by a fascination with fungi and their ecological importance, I'm now
pursuing a **PhD** in the **Global Health Engineering** group at ETH Zürich
(Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering, D-MAVT), led by
Prof. Elizabeth Tilley. My doctoral research explores how filamentous fungi can
be harnessed for sustainable solutions to global health challenges — applying
them in sanitation to reduce pathogens and transform waste into valuable
resources, contributing to the emerging field of **mycosanitation**.

Outside research, I grow fruit and vegetables, cultivate and forage mushrooms,
and hike — deepening my understanding of biology and the natural world along the
way.

See my [research](research.qmd), [software & data](software.qmd), or
[CV](cv.qmd).
